text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: ReservedCapacityThrottle for tenant=VoltWorks (pool=volt-reserved-1) · 70% throttled requests · p95 latency 3.8s · recent errors: 5xx spike. Pager: P1. page_id=PD-44567
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered oncall for eng-oncall (Jamal K). Incident ID PD-44567.
Jamal K: Acked. Looking now. Can someone grab metrics + which squads touched this pool?
Sara P: I pushed canary yesterday but not on volt-reserved-1. That's infra-managed reserved pool.
Anita R: On it — pulling SLO charts and recent deploys.
Leo M: I see a burst of queued requests to that pool from prod region us-west-2 starting +00:02. Batch size spiked. KV cache evictions around same time.
Jamal K: Possible causes: sudden workload spike from VoltWorks or autoscale not kicking. First step: open failover to backup-reserved-2 and increase burst capacity. Who can run the scale command?
OpsBot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/ops/reserved-pool-throttle. Suggested actions: increase_pool_capacity, route_to_backup, notify_customer.
Anita R: Running increase: ```redwoodctl reserved scale --pool volt-reserved-1 --add 2-gpu``` -> queued. ETA ~90s for new capacity to be available.
Leo M: Meanwhile enabling fallback routing for VoltWorks to backup-reserved-2: ```redwoodctl routing set --tenant VoltWorks --fallback backup-reserved-2 --rollout 100%```
Sara P: I'm seeing KV cache eviction rate at 62% which caused regen overhead. If fallback has warmed cache it's good.
Jamal K: Notifying customer success to tell VoltWorks we're on it. @Customer Success please draft message: estimated impact: increased latency and throttles, mitigation in progress.
Customer Success: Drafting now. Can you confirm if any user-facing errors observed?
Leo M: 5xx spike small (~0.2% requests) but p95 latency hurting. No data loss. Mostly slow generations and some token-timeouts.
Anita R: New nodes are up, autoscaler reported allocation succeeded. Adding to pool now.
OpsBot: autoscaler: pool volt-reserved-1 scaled +2 gpus, join completed.
Jamal K: Good. I'm watching metrics. Latency p95 dropping to 1.6s now. Throttles at 12% and falling.
pagerduty: Pager PD-44567 acknowledged by Jamal K at 1769998892.
Oncall_T2: I'm taking secondary. If throttles don't drop under 5% in 10m we'll escalate to infra lead and consider temporary ingress shaping.
Sara P: Can we boot a warm cache job for VoltWorks prefix? That tends to cut regen overhead.
Anita R: Kicking an async prewarm: ```jobs run --type=kvcache_warm --tenant VoltWorks --prefixes=common_prompts```
Jamal K: Customer Success message: "We observed elevated latency and partial throttling for a portion of requests on your reserved pool. Engineers have scaled the pool and routed traffic to a backup pool. Latency is improving; we'll follow up with a post-incident summary." Send now.
Customer Success: Sent to VoltWorks account team.
Leo M: p95 down to 1.2s, throttles 3.1%, errors back to baseline. Stability looks good.
Jamal K: Closing PD-44567? Leave open for 30m monitoring window and then close if stable.
Anita R: Adding notes to incident log and runbook: cause = sudden burst + cache eviction + initial autoscaler lag. Mitigation = scale + fallback + cache prewarm. Action item: tune autoscaler thresholds for reserved pools with known high-burst tenants.
OpsBot: Incident PD-44567: status=monitoring, sla_impact=minor, followup_tasks=[autoscaler-tuning, cache-warm-scripts].
Oncall_T2: I'll own the followup ticket. Jamal, handing off active monitoring to you?
Jamal K: Handoff accepted. I'll monitor next 30m then update. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
